entries.content: S*/Y = S*/(S* + V*), where Y = S* + V* = GFP. The surplus ratio expresses surplus value as a share of the net product (value-added of productive sectors). It is a monotonic transform of the exploitation rate: S*/Y = e/(1+e).
Derived from T505 and T504: S*/Y = T505/(T505 + T504). Presented in Table 5.7 alongside the exploitation rate. No independent extension — follows from T505 and T504 availability.

The surplus ratio is the Marxian analog to the profit share in orthodox economics, but measured only over the productive sector. It rises secularly as the exploitation rate rises, reflecting the increasing proportion of new value captured as surplus rather than wages.

Mohun's employment decomposition and industry classification data (mohun_employment*.csv, mohun_industry_classification.csv) provide alternative frameworks for computing the surplus ratio with different sector boundaries.
No independent extension. The surplus ratio is fully determined by the exploitation rate, so all caveats applying to T506 apply here. Table 5.7 only; no dedicated figure in the book.

DEC-003: The VA*/W constant assumption (ec_u/ec_p ≈ 1.238) propagates directly into T507 because T507 is a monotonic transform of the exploitation rate (T506). The partial resolution in Session 14 (year-varying ec_u/ec_p) reduces but does not eliminate the systematic error. The SIC-era gap (1990-1997) is handled by log-linear interpolation (DEC-007). T507 extension values carry the same systematic error as T506.
